chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Sadah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Among what the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to do in the month of Ramadan was that he would perform voluntary prayers every night, increasing upon the prayer he used to pray before that from the first night until the completion of twenty nights: in each night twenty rak'ahs, eight of them after Maghrib and twelve after the final 'Isha, and he would pray in the last ten nights in each night thirty rak'ahs: twelve of them after Maghrib and eighteen after the final 'Isha, and he would supplicate and strive with intense striving. And he would pray in the night of the twenty-first one hundred rak'ahs, and he would pray in the night of the twenty-third one hundred rak'ahs, and he would strive in them.
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's specific prayer routine during the nights of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) structured escalation in night prayers, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *Qiyam* as a means of spiritual refinement during Ramadan. The specific division of rak'ahs—twenty in the first twenty nights and thirty in the last ten—highlights the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between general voluntary prayers and the intensified devotion of the *Ayyam al-Ghurar* (the first ten days) and *Ayyam al-Wusul* (the last ten days). This practice underscores the theological view that Ramadan is a time for deepening one's connection with the Divine through sustained, incremental worship.
